source_refs.note: Topic 32.3 (PDF 234). The book refers to its Class XI chapter for aspirin; that content is not repeated here.

blocks.text: The mechanism of action is how a drug works at the level of the cell to produce its medical effect. The book names two famous medicines, aspirin and penicillin. The action of aspirin in blocking the COX enzyme was covered in the Class XI book, so this chapter discusses the mechanism of action of penicillin (32.3.1), and then of opiates (32.3.2).

blocks.prompt: What is meant by a drug's mechanism of action?
blocks.explanation: How the drug works at the cellular level to produce its medical effect.

items: Mechanism of action: how a drug works at cell level.
Aspirin blocks the COX enzyme (Class XI); penicillin and opiates follow.
